name: COMBTRAN.jcl
description:
This JCL job (COMBTRAN) combines two transaction sources — a backup transaction file and a system transaction file — into a single unified dataset by sorting them by Transaction ID, and then loads the combined result into a VSAM KSDS file used for card transaction processing.Key Functionalities:
Merges two transaction generation data group (GDG) files — the current backup transaction file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.BKUP generation 0) and the current system transaction file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.SYSTRAN generation 0) — into one combined dataset.
Sorts the merged transactions in ascending order by Transaction ID (TRAN-ID), a 16-character alphanumeric field starting at position 1, ensuring a consistent and ordered transaction sequence.
Writes the sorted, combined transactions to a new GDG generation (+1) of AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.COMBINED, creating a new cataloged sequential dataset on disk.
Reproduces (loads) the newly created combined transaction GDG file into the VSAM KSDS file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS), making the consolidated transactions available for downstream card transaction processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Backup File (current generation) and the System Transaction File (current generation) both exist and are accessible for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction consolidation job is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All transaction records from both the Transaction Backup File and the System Transaction File are combined into a single unified pool of records for further processing

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05R - SORT - Merge Transaction Records from Multiple Sources
rules.Rule_Description: All transaction records from the Transaction Backup File and the System Transaction File are merged together into a single unified pool of transaction data as the first step of consolidation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Transaction records exist in the combined input pool from both the Transaction Backup File and the System Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Transaction records are being processed for sorting and consolidation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each transaction record must be identified by its Transaction ID (TRAN-ID), which is a 16-character text field located at the beginning (position 1 through 16) of every transaction record

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05R - SORT - Transaction ID as the Unique Transaction Identifier
rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is defined as the unique identifier for every transaction record, occupying the first 16 characters of each record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Transaction records from both the Transaction Backup File and the System Transaction File have been merged into a single pool
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The combined pool of transaction records is processed for output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All transaction records must be arranged in ascending order (A to Z, 0 to 9) based on their 16-character Transaction ID (TRAN-ID), so that the resulting Combined Transaction File is fully ordered by Transaction ID

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05R - SORT - Sort All Transactions in Ascending Order by Transaction ID
rules.Rule_Description: All merged transaction records from both sources must be sorted in ascending order using the Transaction ID as the sort key, ensuring a consistent and ordered sequence in the output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The merge and sort of all transaction records from both source files has completed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The sorted and combined transaction records are written to the output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new generation of the Combined Transaction File must be created and permanently saved, while all previously existing generations of the Combined Transaction File are retained and remain accessible for historical reference and audit

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05R - SORT - Create New Generation of Combined Transaction File
rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of the merge and sort process, a new generation of the Combined Transaction File is permanently saved, preserving all prior generations for historical and audit purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new generation of the Combined Transaction File has been initiated during the merge and sort process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The merge and sort process fails or terminates abnormally before successful completion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The newly created generation of the Combined Transaction File must be automatically deleted and must not be retained or cataloged, ensuring that no partial or incomplete transaction data exists in the Combined Transaction File

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05R - SORT - Discard Incomplete Combined Transaction File on Failure
rules.Rule_Description: If the merge and sort process fails for any reason, the newly created generation of the Combined Transaction File must be automatically discarded to prevent any incomplete or partial transaction data from being retained.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A newly created Combined Transaction File (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.COMBINED, latest generation +1) exists and contains all merged and sorted transaction records from both the Transaction Backup File and the System Transaction File, AND the Transaction VSAM KSDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) is available and accessible as the target indexed transaction store
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IDCAMS REPRO utility is executed to copy all records from the Combined Transaction File (TRANSACT) into the Transaction VSAM KSDS (TRANVSAM) without any filtering, selection, or transformation — every record in the source file is transferred as-is to the target VSAM store
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All transaction records from the Combined Transaction File are successfully loaded into the Transaction VSAM KSDS, so that the VSAM store now reflects the most current, complete, and ordered set of all transactions from both source systems, making every transaction immediately available for fast, key-based retrieval by downstream applications using the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) as the key

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Load Combined Transactions into VSAM Transaction Store
rules.Rule_Description: This step refreshes the Transaction VSAM KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Set), which serves as the live indexed transaction repository, by loading all consolidated and sorted transaction records from the newly created Combined Transaction File. Every record is transferred completely without filtering or transformation.
